title: Full-bloom selection gave small estimated spring-slope changes in four US lilac samples in 1965-2008
abstract: We tested whether requiring full-bloom reports changed the first-bloom response to spring warmth in US lilac records from 1965-2008. Four East and West, early and late models compared the same plants with plant and year effects and winter controls. Selected-year minus all-year slopes ranged from -0.043 to +0.006 days per C. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Spring warmth predicted fewer full-bloom reports clearly only in the early western sample. Thus, weather-linked report selection did not give a large estimated change in this slope. This does not prove that missing reports cause no bias. The comparison excludes short plant records and cannot assess unobserved full-bloom dates. Missing visits, coarse weather, different regional plant types and few state clusters limit inference. The package includes exact panels, source hashes, code, all results, and independent coefficient checks.

display.caption: Spring report selection and bloom slopes in four samples. Bars show 98.75% state-cluster intervals. Each four-sample term is a separate family.
